solution_text: Sodium readily loses an electron while chlorine readily gains one, producing Na+ and Cl- ions. Their electrostatic attraction forms an ionic compound.
tips: Large electronegativity differences commonly favor ionic bonding.

solution_text: Molarity is moles of solute divided by volume of solution in litres. M = 0.50/2.0 = 0.25 M.
tips: Convert volume to litres before calculating molarity.

solution_text: The molar mass of H2O is 18 g/mol. Thus, moles = given mass/molar mass = 18/18 = 1 mol.
tips: Use n = mass/molar mass for basic mole calculations.

solution_text: Across a period, effective nuclear charge generally increases while electrons are added to the same principal shell. The stronger attraction pulls the electron cloud closer to the nucleus.
tips: Remember the general periodic trend: atomic radius decreases across a period.
